subject: Sovereign site mapping + warm-standby failover for EU/APAC private deployments
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sovereign site mapping + warm-standby failover for EU/APAC private deployments

Team — putting a draft of the site-mapping and warm-standby failover approach on your radar for the Helios Bank POC and future Private customers in EU / APAC. High level constraints we need to keep front-and-center:

- Data residency: Helios requires EU data-at-rest (primary key material and logs) for EU customers, APAC for APAC customers; no cross-border backups unless expressly consented and logged.
- Failover SLA: target RTO 15m for control-plane health signals, 1h for full model-state rehydration for large models (>100B) unless a reduced-capacity fallback is acceptable.
- Network: customers will prefer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink in-region; for on-prem we need a secure VPN+mutual-TLS pattern for RPC channels.

Attached are: redwood-sovereign-site-map-v1.pdf (draft topology) and a checklist XLS with proposed warm-standby steps. Please review the following questions and reply inline:

1) Site selection: do we recommend a cold-region (object storage only) + warm-standby compute region per geography, or active-active with synchronous metadata replication? Pros/cons for Helios?
2) KV cache & model shards: acceptable to keep KV caches ephemeral in standby and rely on prefix-caching on failover? Impact to RTO?
3) Operational runbook: what minimum telemetry/trace retention do we need in-region to meet audit requests while keeping costs reasonable?

I'm aiming to finalize recommendations by EOD Wed so we can send to Helios and CloudPartner APAC ahead of Thurs sync.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sovereign site mapping + warm-standby failover for EU/APAC private deployments

Kimberly — quick thoughts after skimming the PDF and checklist. I think a hybrid approach is better: warm-standby compute + cross-region object replication but with encrypted-at-rest keys scoped to region. Details below.

- Site selection: recommend one active region per legal boundary (e.g., EU-West for EU, APAC-SE for APAC) with a warm-standby in a nearby jurisdiction for latency-cost tradeoffs. Warm-standby means instances spun up but kept at reduced capacity (e.g., 1/4 replicas) with autoscale triggers. This minimizes RTO versus cold-only solutions.
- Sync model artifacts: use object-store replication (async) + write-ahead manifest that is signed and stored in-region. On failover, we replay manifest to reconstruct model bundle; for very large quantized artifacts we can support chunked parallel fetch to speed rehydration.
- KV cache: make it ephemeral on standby. To reduce RTO, maintain a small region-local prefix cache for high-frequency keys (hot prompts) and rely on model to regen lower-frequency content. This should keep the 15m control-plane goal realistic.
- Network: prefer PrivateLink for hosted customers; for on-prem, we must advise customers to host a transit gateway that supports BGP for routing and have mutual-TLS for our control plane.

Open questions: what are Helios's capacity sloshed for failover (expected qps if EU primary fails)? That drives replica sizing. Also need legal signoff on KMS configuration (separate CMKs per region or single multi-region key).

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
From: Helios Bank <infra@heliosbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Sovereign site mapping + warm-standby failover for EU/APAC private deployments

Thanks Kimberly and Jonas — useful starting point. A few clarifying items from our side before Thurs sync: 

1) Customer SLAs: Helios can accept warm-standby if we can preserve customer-level logs and audit trails in-region with immutable retention for 7 years. Can you confirm whether Redwood will keep audit logs and KMS audit trails strictly in-region and provide tamper-evident delivery?
2) Failover capacity: if EU primary is unavailable, Helios requires at least 40% of steady-state throughput in-region within 30 minutes for critical banking workflows. Full capacity within 6 hours is acceptable for non-critical workloads.
3) Data transport during failover: must be encrypted in transit with customer-controlled keys where possible and logged. We also need a short description of how you will avoid cross-border transfer of PII during the failover bootstrap.

Happy to share a short appendix with legal constraints — I'll attach it before the call.

- Rakesh Malhotra
VP, Infrastructure Operations
Helios Bank
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: infra@heliosbank.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: eng@cloudpartner-apac.io
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sovereign site mapping + warm-standby failover for EU/APAC private deployments

Rakesh — thanks for the clear constraints, that helps. Short answers and next steps from our side: 

- Audit logs + KMS: we will provision region-scoped CMKs (customer-specific CMK per legal region) and keep KMS audit logs and model access logs in-region. Tamper-evidence will be provided via signed manifests and hash chains (we've included a comms-runbook-diff.txt that highlights the signed-manifest flow).
- Capacity & RTO: we can commit to a warm-standby topology that achieves ~40% of steady-state in-region within 30 minutes for critical queues by maintaining 1/3 active replicas + autoscale thresholds tuned to failover signals. Full capacity rebuild (model rehydration) target: 4–6 hours for largest quantized artifacts; for customers needing faster full-capacity we can propose partial model-splitting to enable earlier progression of latency-sensitive features.
- Cross-border PII: during failover we will avoid transferring unencrypted PII by ensuring that any state transfer is metadata-first (signed manifests) and that decrypted blobs are only materialized in-region under the customer's CMK. If Helios wants, we can add an optional step to force customer-side rekeying before failover to ensure key authority stays local.

Action items:
- Jonas: update the warm-standby checklist with replica sizing for 40% RTO target and add BGP/PrivateLink wiring diagrams (due Thu 12:00 PT).
- Marcus: prepare KMS key-per-region configuration options and a short pros/cons brief for Helios legal (due Thu 12:00 PT).
- Kimberly: assemble a 2-page summary for Helios call on Thu with the topology, the signed-manifest flow, and the runbook excerpt (I will send by Wed morning EU time).

I've attached the three artifacts to the thread. If nothing else, we'll push this to the Thurs sync and capture any policy/contract asks.

Best —
Kimberly Park
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
